paper_metadata.title: Novel eutectic refractory high entropy alloys with superior mechanical performance

evidence.quote: Novel eutectic refractory high entropy alloys with superior mechanical performance

other.raw_materials_purity: Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti > 99.95 wt%; TiC > 99.9 %

evidence.quote: The MoNbTaTiC x (...) samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting a mixture of corresponding metal (Mo, Nb, Ta and Ti) with a purity higher than 99.95 wt% and TiC with a purity higher than 99.9 % in water-cooled copper crucibles under high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure a homogeneous distribution of elements, all samples were flipped after each melt and remelted for 5 times.

The alloy reached a fully eutectic morphology at x = 0.5. This morphology consisted of a eutectic colony where the two phases were formed alternatively (see Fig. 2 (e)).

Eutectic morphology with an alternate lamellar structure is proved to be an effective way to achieve good combination of ductility and strength at the same time, due to high volume fraction of strengthening phase, good interface bonding, and various interfaces which could accommodate more dislocations in the deformation process

Therefore, the MNTTC0.5 alloy with a fully eutectic microstructure has similar fracture strain compared with MNTTC0.4 alloy while owing higher strength, leading many typical RHEAs which are robust at high temperatures.
